evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We ran a cluster RCT of community health worker home-visit reminders for antenatal iron-folate adherence in 24 health centers in Mchinji and Dedza, Malawi (12 per arm), 1,600 women enrolled at treatment centers over 10 months in 2025. Effect from our pre-specified model: adherence (pill count of 80% or more at 32 weeks) was 43% vs 31%, +12 percentage points (95% CI 5 to 19). Costs: 48 CHWs spent about 4 hours a week for 40 weeks (they are government-stipended, we did not pay them; local wage about $0.75/hour); 4 supervisors 8 hours a month for 10 months at $2.50/hour; a 2-day training for 52 people cost $2,600; 48 bicycles at $90 each (3-year life); printed adherence cards $0.20 each; phone credit $2 per CHW per month; monthly CHW meetings used clinic rooms for free (about $5 a meeting at 24 centers); data entry $600; endline survey and pill counts for the trial $9,000. No cash or in-kind transfers. The ministry wants to compare us with an SMS-only reminder program in another district, per additional adherent woman. Program perspective. USD 2025, average market rate.
evals.expected_output: A cost-effectiveness estimate in the output template giving the cost per additional adherent woman, with its sensitivity rows.
assertions: Prices the health workers' time at the local wage although the program did not pay it, and spreads the bicycle cost over its useful life.
Keeps the $9,000 survey and pill-count cost out of the delivery total.
Divides by about 192 additional adherent women, not by all 1,600 women.
Reruns the ratio at the 5- and 19-point confidence bounds.
States the perspective, the currency year, and the discount rate.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: What's the cost-effectiveness of our SMS program? The budget was $40,000.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the effect and for the costs the budget leaves out, and produces no ratio.
assertions: Asks for the effect estimate with its confidence interval.
Asks for inputs used but not paid for, or which costs were research.
Does not divide the $40,000 by any number.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our community health agents in Lusaka, Zambia sold condoms door to door; the trial found +310 condoms sold per agent per quarter (CI 120 to 500) across 80 agents, and we have a full ingredients list in USD 2025 with no transfers. The ministry wants to decide next week whether to fund this or the antenatal visit program in Copperbelt, which reported a cost per additional antenatal visit. Can you give us a single number that says which program is the better buy?
evals.expected_output: The skill estimates the condom program's cost per additional condom sold, declines to rank the two programs, and names an economist.
assertions: Gives a cost per additional condom sold, rerun at the 120 and 500 bounds.
Declines to give one number ranking the two programs.
Says the programs have different outcomes, so ranking them needs a value on each outcome or the ministry's own weights.
Tells the user to consult a health or development economist before the funding decision.
Says what to bring to that specialist.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We have our cost per additional fully immunized child from the Rajasthan-style camp pilot in two blocks. The state government now wants to run it across the whole district with its own staff. Will the cost per child hold?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the estimate exists and the question is whether it survives scale-up with a new implementer, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the question is whether the cost holds at scale with a different implementer.
Does not recompute the cost per child.
